Special posting considerations: The intent of this process is to staff two (2) positions: one (1) 24-month term appointment with the possibility of extension, acting, assignment, secondment, or exchange and one (1) indeterminate appointment. This process also aims to create a pool of partially and fully qualified candidates that may be used to staff similar term or indeterminate positions within both Agencies.
Candidates must clearly demonstrate in their cover letter how they meet the education and experience factors listed in the essential and asset qualifications. The cover letter should not exceed two (2) pages in English or two and half (2.5) pages in French* (8.5x11; 11 point font; normal margins). Please note that it is not sufficient to only state that the qualification is met; applicants must clearly indicate how they meet the merit criteria by providing concrete examples. Resumes will be used as a secondary source to validate the experience described in the cover letter. Failure to clearly demonstrate in your cover letter how you meet the screening criteria (education and experience) will result in the rejection of your application. Candidates will not be solicited for incomplete or possible missing information.
*The additional length of French cover letters recognizes anticipated differences in length to express similar content based on official language choice.
Who we are
This position falls within a directorate that provides common services to two funding agencies: the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) and the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC).
At the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC), we bring together the research community, as well as the public, private and not-for-profit sectors, in contributing knowledge, talent and expertise to build a better future for Canada and the world. SSHRC is seeking talented professionals passionate about Canadian research and the value it brings to society.
The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) is Canada’s largest funder of science and engineering. A career at NSERC means supporting the visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will advance knowledge, improve the lives of Canadians and transform the world for the better.
Visit our career page at SSHRC or NSERC to learn more about why you should join our agency.
What you will do
As an Evaluation Manager, your responsibilities will include:
Leadership and direction in the delivery of performance measurement, evaluation and review services including the provision of strategic and authoritative advice to senior management of the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC)‘s, Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)’s and Inter-Agency programs and other external stakeholders to optimize the effective and sound evaluation, assessment, and analysis of the performance of NSERC’s, SSHRC’s and Inter-Agency programs and associated policies.
What you need to succeed
Education
- Master’s degree from a recognized university with a specialisation in evaluation, economics, sociology, statistics, or social sciences research methods, OR an acceptable combination of education, training, and relevant work experience with a specialization in one of these fields. A graduate diploma in program evaluation would also be acceptable.
- Foreign Credential Validation against Canadian Standards
Experience
- Extensive 1 experience conducting evaluations of programs, including those involving multiple organizations, consistent with the Federal Government’s policies related to evaluation.
- Extensive 1 experience applying a range of evaluation methods, including both qualitative and quantitative techniques.
- Experience supervising or managing human resources.
- Extensive 1 experience analyzing data, synthesizing evaluation findings and presenting results to senior management.
- Experience evaluating research or research related activities, and/or grants and contribution programs would be an asset .
1 Extensive is equivalent to five (5) or more years of experience.
Knowledge
- Knowledge of program evaluation theory and practices, including federal government performance measurement and evaluation policies/standards.
- Knowledge of evaluation methods and approaches, including qualitative and quantitative analysis techniques.
- Knowledge of project management principles.
- Knowledge of the post-secondary research funding environment, the research process and the transfer of research results to the user sector would be an asset .
Competencies
- Client service and delivery oriented.
- Analytical thinking (analysis and problem-solving).
- Effective oral and written communication.
- Demonstrate initiative and flexibility, and act with confidence.
Key Leadership Competencies
- Create Vision and Strategy.
- Mobilize People.
- Uphold integrity and respect.
- Collaboration with Partners and Stakeholders.
- Promote Innovation and Guide Change.
- Achieve Results.
Equity, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to inclusive and barrier-free recruitment to create a workforce that reflects the Canadians we serve. We promote employment equity and encourage you to indicate if you belong to one of the designated groups when you apply.
We welcome all candidates, and encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Métis and Inuit), veterans, persons with disabilities, Black and other racialized persons, persons of ethnic origins, diverse religions, abilities, sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.
Accommodation
Let our team know if you require accommodation or support during the recruitment process by contacting us at recruiting@nserc-crsng.gc.ca .
If you require additional information on the position, please contact us at recruiting@nserc-crsng.gc.ca .

About CMHC
The work you do and the work we do together matters. We come to work every day with a common purpose: to contribute to a well-functioning housing system.
At CMHC, we hold ourselves accountable for our results and support our colleagues in their achievements. We thrive on collaboration, connecting across CMHC and involving the right people to get our work done. Our leadership style is guided by trust , where our leaders favour an adaptive approach based on the needs of their teams.
Join us and be part of a team that's committed to making a real difference and be part of something meaningful.
What’s in it for you
We’ve got the purpose, the people and the perks you need for a fulfilling career. Here’s the comprehensive and generous benefits you get when you’re a contract employee:
- Accrued vacation.
- Annual individual performance bonus.
- Support towards your personal and professional growth with training, mentorship and more.
- An inclusive workplace culture and environment.
About the role
Join the Accounting Operations and Procurement team, in the Team Leader, Cash Management position. In this role, you will lead and manage a team responsible for cash receipt application, collections, account reconciliations, and the reporting of banking transactions. You will provide guidance to clients on financial operating requirements and processes, helping them navigate complex financial matters and enabling informed business decisions. You will develop a deep understanding of business operations through analysis, collaboration, and stakeholder engagement, allowing you to identify financial needs, build trusted relationships, and deliver valuable business insights. As a subject matter expert, you will lead process improvement initiatives to optimize accounting and reporting processes while supporting ongoing transformation and modernization efforts across the organization.
This is a temporary position of a duration of 12 months.
What you’ll do:
- Lead and manage a team responsible for cash receipts, cash applications, collections, account reconciliations, banking transactions, and related financial reporting activities.
- Oversee the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of accounting records, reconciliations, and financial reports, ensuring compliance with accounting standards, policies, and regulatory requirements.
- Analyze complex financial information, identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and provide recommendations that support sound business decision-making.
- Provide guidance to clients on financial operations, accounting processes, budgeting considerations, and financial controls.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with internal stakeholders and business leaders, developing a deep understanding of operational needs to deliver value-added financial insights and solutions.
- Lead continuous improvement initiatives by identifying process inefficiencies, implementing innovative solutions, and optimizing accounting, reporting, and operational processes.
- Monitor the effectiveness of accounting policies, systems, and internal controls, identifying control gaps and recommending corrective actions to strengthen financial governance.
- Support audits and financial oversight activities by ensuring the timely preparation of reports, analyses, explanations, and supporting documentation.
- Develop, coach, and empower team members by setting clear expectations, providing ongoing feedback, fostering accountability, and promoting an inclusive and high-performing work environment.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in a related field such as accounting, finance, business administration, economics, or commerce.
- A minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience in accounting with a minimum of 1 year of supervisory/ project leadership experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
- An extensive knowledge of accounting principles, financial statements, and applicable financial, legislative, and regulatory requirements.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to gather and synthesize complex information and develop practical, well-supported recommendations.
- Experience with financial systems and software applications, combined with advanced computer skills and a strong aptitude for leveraging technology to support business objectives.
- A demonstrated success leading teams, providing coaching and feedback, and fostering a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing work environment.
- A proven experience driving process improvements, increasing operational efficiencies, and implementing solutions that support evolving business needs.
- Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and client service skills, with the ability to influence, negotiate, and effectively engage stakeholders at all levels of an organization.
It would be great if you also had:
- An MBA.
- A Professional accounting designation (CPA).
- Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Financial Operations (ERP Software).
- A Six Sigma certification.
Posting closing date: Note, the competition will remain active until filled.
Our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion
We’re committed to employment equity and encourage women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, veterans and persons of all races, ethnicities, religions, abilities, sexual orientations, and gender identities and expressions to apply. We also welcome applications from non-Canadians who are eligible to work in Canada.
CMHC is an inclusive workplace where diversity of thought – and of people – are recognized, valued, and considered essential to achieving our mission.
Learn more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion
What happens after you apply
We know that applying for a new job can be both exciting and daunting, and we appreciate your effort. Learn more about our hiring process . If you are selected for an interview or testing, please advise us if you require an accommodation.
If you applied before and you were not successful don’t worry – we're always posting new positions, so don’t hesitate to give it another shot. We’re excited to see what you bring to the table this time around!

About the role Join the Multi-Unit Insurance Servicing (MUIS) team, in the Bilingual Senior Officer, Operations position. The MUIS team supports Approved Lenders throughout the life of insured multi-unit mortgage loans by administering servicing requests, covenant changes, borrower structure updates, and other post-funding matters. In this role, you will review and analyze servicing requests, assess risk, provide recommendations, and work closely with lenders and internal partners to ensure timely and consistent service delivery. This position offers an opportunity to develop expertise in mortgage loan insurance servicing while contributing to CMHC's commitment to supporting a stable and sustainable housing system.
What you’ll do:
- Review, analyze and process servicing requests related to insured multi-unit mortgage loans, identify risks and issues, and provide recommendations in accordance with CMHC policies and insurance requirements.
- Analyze borrower, property, and financial information to support recommendations and decision-making.
- Communicate with lenders to obtain additional information, clarify requirements, and provide guidance on servicing processes.
- Prepare recommendations and escalate more complex issues to management, as required.
- Maintain accurate documentation and records to support decisions and ensure file completeness.
- Respond to lender inquiries in a professional, timely, and client-focused manner.

The role
We are looking for a conscientious, solutions-oriented English Technical Editor who strives for excellence to support our Construction Research Centre. The English Technical Editor would be someone who shares our core values of impact, accountability, leadership, integrity and collaboration.
The national model construction codes—collectively referred to as “Codes Canada”—are developed through a collaborative process involving the best expertise from across Canada and around the world to provide effective building and safety regulations that are harmonized across Canada.
These highly legalistic and technically complex documents are accessed by thousands of practitioners in the construction industry, so the standards of quality are very high.
The incumbent provides English technical editing, copyediting, proofreading and electronic (XML, Microsoft Word, Adobe Acrobat) input services for the production and publication of the national and provincial construction codes (quasi-judicial, technical documents), user's guides, intent statements, information documents, specifications, and promotional material.
The incumbent is responsible for ensuring that English publications and documents are clear, logical and accurate, and conform to accepted standards of style, grammar and usage.
The incumbent works on site within a team of editors, translators and IT specialists

- Experience in editing and proofreading communications materials, promotional brochures, factsheets, ads, and social media messaging in English.
- Experience in planning and scheduling editorial and document production tasks and carrying them out within tight deadlines.

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are looking for an Assistant Shift Operating Engineer to support our Real Property Planning and Management Branch. The incumbent would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity. Our Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA) registered First Class High-Pressure Power Plant operates with a small team of Operating Engineers who are typically designated as Shift Operating Engineer and Assistant Shift Operating Engineer. The Operating team operates on a rotational 12-hour shift basis (24 hours/day, 7 days/week, 365 days/year). Under the direction of the Assistant Chief Operating Engineer, the Assistant Shift Operating Engineer would be responsible for all maintenance related to the boiler room, air compressors, chillers, gas turbine and steam distribution to the NRC Main campus located on Montreal Road. The incumbent is also responsible for the water treatment of open and closed loops. They are also called upon to provide support for the Shift Operating Engineers as required. Steam production is provided by 4 boilers with an additional boost from the Heat Recovery Steam generator (HRSG) given the cogeneration aspect. The gas turbine generator forms the basis of the cogeneration having an electrical power output of 4.5 MW. This is a unique installation within a Federal Government facility setting. As a federal employer, the NRC offers a great pension plan, medical and dental benefits and leave provision (3 weeks vacation, sick leave, family-related, personal leave) and also great opportunities for career growth within the Real Property Management and Planning Branch.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Successful completion of secondary school according to provincial standards. Must have a valid Third Class Operating Engineer Certificate issued by the Technical Standards and Safety Authority (TSSA) .
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Experience working in a complex, high-pressure steam plant.
- Experience performing necessary maintenance and tests, keeping records and responding to power or equipment failures.
The following experience criteria would be considered an asset:
- Experience operating in a first-class plant.
- Experience with gas turbine co-generation.
Condition of employment
- Must be available to work on rotating 12 hour shifts as the heating plant operates 24/7.
- Must be able to possess and retain the physical capabilities to perform the position which include but may not be limited to: crouching, bending, twisting, walking, climbing stairs & ladders, ability to hear to diagnose mechanical troubles, and the ability to handle heavy and bulky objects.
- Must be able to obtain and retain a Third Class Operating Engineer Certificate issued by TSSA.
- Reliability Status
For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Knowledge of operating and maintenance procedures related to the operation of a high-pressure steam and co-generation (gas turbine) plant and its distribution systems.
- Knowledge of electrical generation.
- Knowledge of boiler water treatment and cooling tower water treatment applicable to the occupation.
Behavioural competencies
- Management services - Client focus (Level 1)
- Management services - Communication (Level 1)
- Management services - Conceptual and analytical ability (Level 1)
- Management services - Results orientation (Level 1)
- Management services - Teamwork (Level 1)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Management Services .
View all competency profiles

From $78,227 to $82,104 per annum.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.

- Willingness to work in confined spaces.

About the position We are seeking an innovative and dedicated individual to join the Sector Resilience and Strategic Partnerships team within the Cyber Security Division!
Reporting to the Assistant Director - Sector Resilience and Strategic Partnerships, you will work with financial sector participants and stakeholders across the Bank to support:
- The Canadian Financial Sector Resiliency Group (CFRG), Canada's public-private sector coordination forum focused on systemic operational resilience, crisis preparedness and coordination.
- The Canadian Financial Authorities Cyber and Technology Forum (CFACT), which brings together federal financial authorities to strengthen cyber and technology risk management, information sharing, and coordinated preparedness activities.
- The G7 Cyber Experts Group (CEG), an international forum that strengthens cyber resilience, sector preparedness, crisis coordination, and collective responses to emerging risks affecting the global financial system.
This role provides a unique opportunity to develop deep expertise in financial sector resilience, gain insight into industry and government perspectives, and contribute directly to collective action initiatives that strengthen the resilience of Canada's financial system.
We offer many opportunities for career development and mentorship – both within and outside of Cyber.
As a part of the team, you will have the full support of your leader to enhance your skills, experiment, learn and strive in a constantly evolving environment.
What you will do You will be a member of the Secretariat to support Canadian Financial Sector Resiliency Group (CFRG), Canadian Financial Authorities Cyber and Technology Forum (CFACT), and G7 Cyber Experts Group.
You will support the planning, governance, execution, and continuous improvement of sector resilience initiatives and work with participants across Canada's financial system.
More specifically, you will:
- Support the secretariat functions of CFRG, CFACT, and G7 CEG, including governance, briefing materials, meeting coordination, and stakeholder engagement.
- Engage directly with participants from Canada's largest financial institutions, financial market infrastructures, government agencies, and international partners through meetings, workshops, exercises, and collaborative initiatives.
- Lead program management activities, including workplans, risk and issue management, action tracking, and reporting.
- Develop executive briefings, presentations, reports, and communications for senior leaders and external stakeholders.
- Support sector resilience initiatives focused on cyber resilience, operational resilience, emerging technology risks (including artificial intelligence), financial stability considerations, and sector crisis coordination through exercises and preparedness activities.
- Contribute to the development, testing, and continuous improvement of sector coordination mechanisms used to support information sharing and collective response during major cyber and operational incidents affecting Canada's financial sector.
- Build and maintain strong partnerships across the financial sector and coordinate sector working groups to advance resilience objectives across Canada's financial system.
What you need to succeed You are a strong relationship builder with excellent critical thinking, communication, and organizational skills. You thrive in collaborative environments, are comfortable engaging with senior leaders and external stakeholders, and can effectively manage competing priorities in a dynamic environment.
In addition, you have:
- Experience supporting governance forums, strategic initiatives, program delivery, business analysis, or other analytical functions.
- Experience building partnerships across multiple organizations, gathering stakeholder requirements, analyzing complex issues, and developing practical recommendations.
- Experience preparing briefing materials, reports, presentations, and communications for executive and external audiences.
Nice-to-have
- Knowledge of Canada's financial system, financial stability, wholesale payments, or regulatory and policy frameworks.
- Knowledge of operational resilience, cyber resilience, crisis management, incident response, risk management, or sector coordination mechanisms.
- Knowledge of emerging technology risks (including artificial intelligence), third-party risk, cloud services, or critical infrastructure.
- Cybersecurity experience is not required, as this is a development opportunity.
Your education and experience Your combined education and work experience demonstrate that you have the competencies and skills for the position. We are ideally seeking candidates with a degree in public policy, economics, information systems, risk management, cyber security, or a related discipline, together with 7+ years of experience supporting governance forums, stakeholder engagement, resilience programs, strategic initiatives, or program delivery.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.

If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.

Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. This position provides expert advice on enforcement and operational matters, conducts research and analysis to inform decision-making, and collaborates with internal and external stakeholders through national and local working groups to address issues, advance initiatives, and promote the consistent application of screening procedures across the organization. The Senior Advisor, Operational Procedures performs all other duties and responsibilities related to the position as required.

- A minimum of six (6) years of experience providing strategic advice and developing a wide range of materials, including briefing notes or presentations for senior management review and approval.

- Highly collaborative team player with the ability to build productive working relationships and contribute effectively to a multidisciplinary environment.
- Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy and quality.

Join the Infrastructure and Operations team, in the Bilingual Advisor, Cloud Infrastructure Design and Engineering position.
The Advisor, Cloud Infrastructure Design and Engineering is a senior technical authority responsible for defining, governing, and continuously improving the organization’s cloud and infrastructure platforms across public cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments. The role ensures infrastructure solutions align with business objectives, IT strategy, security, operational requirements, and enterprise standards by establishing cloud architecture principles, design standards, reusable patterns, reference implementations, and governance guardrails.
Acting as the technical design lead, the Advisor translates business and technical requirements into scalable, secure, resilient, observable, automated, and cost-effective cloud solutions, while shaping cloud strategy, target-state architectures, modernization roadmaps, and major technology investments. Working closely with infrastructure leadership and cross-functional teams, the Advisor provides expert guidance on cloud services, platform selection, design trade-offs, and operational readiness, setting the technical direction for how cloud platforms are adopted, integrated, secured, and operated across the enterprise to drive consistent, sustainable, and high-performing infrastructure outcomes.
What you’ll do:
- Evaluate emerging cloud services, infrastructure platforms, and technologies to support business objectives, operational needs, and future-state architecture.
- Conduct technical, operational, risk, and cost analyses to inform cloud strategy, infrastructure roadmaps, and investment decisions.

- Ensure all cloud and infrastructure designs comply with security, privacy, risk, resilience, regulatory, and OSFI requirements, while continuously identifying opportunities for improvement.
- Research, validate, pilot, and recommend new technologies, vendors, and services, while contributing to cloud and infrastructure strategy and modernization initiatives.
- Define, govern, and enforce cloud infrastructure standards, design principles, reference architectures, reusable patterns, policies, operational guardrails, and API platform requirements.
- Establish secure and scalable foundations for AI platforms, including landing zones, networking, identity, access controls, data access patterns, observability, and compliance requirements.
- Provide senior technical leadership through design governance, the Cloud Infrastructure Design Forum, mentoring, stakeholder influence, risk management, and trusted advisory support across infrastructure, platform, security, application, and delivery teams.
What you should have:
- A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience).
- At least 10+ years of IT experience, including 5+ years in senior technical roles, with a proven track record of delivering enterprise-scale solutions, architecture, and technical roadmaps.
- An extensive expertise in Azure, cloud infrastructure, and hybrid environments, including cloud platform design, validation, governance, and operations.
- A strong knowledge of application platforms, middleware, virtualization, Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS), Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), capacity planning, and platform architecture.
- A hands-on experience with Docker, Kubernetes, Linux/UNIX environments (e.g., Red Hat, AIX), and designing scalable, resilient containerized platforms.
- An experience enabling DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure automation, and cloud-native engineering practices.
- A deep understanding of enterprise networking, data platforms, database infrastructure, cloud security, identity and access management, encryption, monitoring, compliance, and resiliency.
- An expertise in designing and governing AI platform infrastructure and API management platforms (e.g., Azure AI Services, Azure API Management), including landing zones, networking, RBAC, security, scalability, observability, operational supportability, and governance.

About the role
Join the Infrastructure and Operations team, in the Advisor, Cloud Infrastructure Design and Engineering position.
The Advisor, Cloud Infrastructure Design and Engineering is a senior technical authority responsible for defining, governing, and continuously improving the organization’s cloud and infrastructure platforms across public cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments. The role ensures infrastructure solutions align with business objectives, IT strategy, security, operational requirements, and enterprise standards by establishing cloud architecture principles, design standards, reusable patterns, reference implementations, and governance guardrails.
Acting as the technical design lead, the Advisor translates business and technical requirements into scalable, secure, resilient, observable, automated, and cost-effective cloud solutions, while shaping cloud strategy, target-state architectures, modernization roadmaps, and major technology investments. Working closely with infrastructure leadership and cross-functional teams, the Advisor provides expert guidance on cloud services, platform selection, design trade-offs, and operational readiness, setting the technical direction for how cloud platforms are adopted, integrated, secured, and operated across the enterprise to drive consistent, sustainable, and high-performing infrastructure outcomes.
What you’ll do:
- Evaluate emerging cloud services, infrastructure platforms, and technologies to support business objectives, operational needs, and future-state architecture.
- Conduct technical, operational, risk, and cost analyses to inform cloud strategy, infrastructure roadmaps, and investment decisions.
- Design cloud-centric solutions that balance security, scalability, resiliency, availability, supportability, performance, and cost optimization in collaboration with key stakeholders.
- Ensure all cloud and infrastructure designs comply with security, privacy, risk, resilience, regulatory, and OSFI requirements, while continuously identifying opportunities for improvement.
- Research, validate, pilot, and recommend new technologies, vendors, and services, while contributing to cloud and infrastructure strategy and modernization initiatives.
- Define, govern, and enforce cloud infrastructure standards, design principles, reference architectures, reusable patterns, policies, operational guardrails, and API platform requirements.
- Establish secure and scalable foundations for AI platforms, including landing zones, networking, identity, access controls, data access patterns, observability, and compliance requirements.
- Provide senior technical leadership through design governance, the Cloud Infrastructure Design Forum, mentoring, stakeholder influence, risk management, and trusted advisory support across infrastructure, platform, security, application, and delivery teams.
What you should have:
- A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience).
- At least 10+ years of IT experience, including 5+ years in senior technical roles, with a proven track record of delivering enterprise-scale solutions, architecture, and technical roadmaps.
- An extensive expertise in Azure, cloud infrastructure, and hybrid environments, including cloud platform design, validation, governance, and operations.
- A strong knowledge of application platforms, middleware, virtualization, Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS), Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), capacity planning, and platform architecture.
- A hands-on experience with Docker, Kubernetes, Linux/UNIX environments (e.g., Red Hat, AIX), and designing scalable, resilient containerized platforms.
- An experience enabling DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure automation, and cloud-native engineering practices.
- A deep understanding of enterprise networking, data platforms, database infrastructure, cloud security, identity and access management, encryption, monitoring, compliance, and resiliency.
- An expertise in designing and governing AI platform infrastructure and API management platforms (e.g., Azure AI Services, Azure API Management), including landing zones, networking, RBAC, security, scalability, observability, operational supportability, and governance.

Who we are
At the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC), we bring together the research community, as well as the public, private and not-for-profit sectors, in contributing knowledge, talent and expertise to build a better future for Canada and the world. The Communications Advisor develops implements and evaluates communications plans and activities to promote Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC) and/or Tri-agency policies, priorities, programs and/or initiatives. Together with the position’s immediate supervisor, develops and implements approaches, strategies and positioning for SSHRC and its programs, and offers communications advice and support to internal clients. Works with universities and other stakeholders and partners to promote SSHRC activities, including organization of media and promotional events.

Education

- Experience in planning and organizing events for external audiences that meet strategic communications objectives, including conferences and workshops, ministerial announcements, news conferences, media briefings and promotional activities.

- Experience coordinating internal and change communication strategies or plans.
- Experience in emergency or crisis communications.

- Knowledge of digital marketing communications techniques
- Knowledge of best practices in organizational and corporate communications
Competencies
- Analytical thinking

The Coordinator, Construction Services, manages and administers medium-complexity construction, professional services and service contracts during construction to ensure compliance with contract requirements. The incumbent engages in daily discussions and negotiations with contractors, consultants and the Client-Partners about quality of work, interpretation of contract documents, scope changes, progress claim reviews and other issues. The incumbent addresses contract management risks within delegated authority, complies with service line requirements, and integrates activities with site teams and other service lines.
KEY AND PERIODIC ACTIVITIES The duties and responsibilities listed below are representative but not all-inclusive: Primary
- Manage and administer contracts to ensure compliance with contractual requirements and quality specifications
- Coordinate and solve day-to-day contractual problems
- Monitor and control schedules
- Liaise with Client-Partner representatives (e.g. on contract-related problems and risks, negotiate and issue change orders)
- Maintain site activity records (e.g. photos, activity reports)
- Liaise with other service lines and site teams, as required
- Develop and maintain effective relationships within DCC, and with industry, the Client Partners and/or stakeholders
- Ensure quality standards are met, in line with corporate and Client-Partner expectations
- Manage contract risks
Other
- Manage contract financials
- Coordinate consultant construction review and third-party testing
- Ensure health and safety, industrial security and environmental compliance
- Support and/or lead business development activities
- Other duties as assigned

- Best practices, methods, trends and legislation in construction
- Construction, products and materials
- Project, contract and risk management principles
- Health and safety management
Formal Education and/or Certification(s) and Experience
- Minimum: college diploma in engineering, applied science or related field with four years’ relevant experience, or the equivalent
- Preferred: certification in applicable field (e.g. Certified Engineering Technologist)
Abilities
- Use applicable computer software and operating systems
- Interpret drawings and specifications
- Apply project, contract and risk management techniques to construction and consultant contracts
DEVELOPMENT AND LEADERSHIP
- Provide functional advice and guidance to employees and to Client-Partners

- Typical construction site environment; incumbent is required to wear basic safety equipment
- Some work may be in a typical office environment with occasional travel

Your package includes:

- 100% employer-paid annual sick leave, and health and dental premiums
- $400 wellness allowance to help cover expenses such as a gym membership
- $2,500 for mental health services on top of regular $2,500 paramedical coverage
- Telus Virtual Health Care and $750 Health Care Spending Account for some expenses not covered under provincial plans

- Life, accidental-death, and short-term disability insurance
- Enhanced inConfidence employee and family assistance program
- Maternity and parental leave top-up plan to 93% of regular gross earnings for up to 37 weeks

- Public-service pension

To begin a career with Defence Construction Canada (DCC), you must be a Canadian Citizen or a permanent resident of Canada. As a condition of employment with DCC, a minimum reliability security status clearance is required and some roles may require secret security status clearance.
DCC is responsible for the Personnel Security Clearance process . Typically to be eligible for a "Reliability" clearance, you must have five years of verifiable background information and to be eligible for a "Secret" clearance, you must have 10 years of verifiable background information. The process usually involves reference inquiries, verification of qualifications, criminal records checks, and credit checks (as required) and may require fingerprints. For more information about obtaining a security clearance, please review the Standard on Security Screening .
The appropriate security clearance is a condition of employment and it is the candidate’s or employee’s responsibility to ensure, they are able to obtain and maintain their required security level clearance to begin or continue their employment with DCC. About the role
Join the Compliance Office team, in the Senior Specialist, Compliance and Risk Governance position, where you will contribute to strengthening CMHC's relationship with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) through ongoing engagement on compliance, governance, and risk management matters. In this role, you will provide expert support in interpreting and assessing OSFI expectations, helping business areas understand regulatory requirements and align practices, controls, and governance processes accordingly.
You will work closely with stakeholders across CMHC to support the proactive management of regulatory issues, and contribute to the development and implementation of remediation and improvement initiatives. Drawing on your knowledge of compliance and risk governance, you will help ensure that regulatory considerations are effectively integrated into business decision-making, reporting, and governance processes. Through these activities, you will support the effectiveness of the Three Lines Model, contribute to strong corporate governance, and promote a culture of sound risk management in support of CMHC's business objectives and strategic priorities.
What you'll do:
- Serve as the primary liaison with OSFI, maintaining effective relationships and ensring timely, accurate, and consistent responses through collaboration with business lines and oversight functions.
- Provide guidance on OSFI regulatory expectations and internal governance frameworks, supporting business lines in strengthening risk posture and promoting a culture of regulatory compliance, accountability, and risk awareness.
- Provide second line oversight by monitoring alignment with OSFI guidance and internal frameworks, identifying gaps or control deficiencies, recommending corrective actions, and supporting policy and framework enhancements.
- Lead the development and implementation of OSFI regulatory compliance and risk governance review cycles and coordinate three-lines-of-defence oversight planning to ensure focus on areas of highest risk.
- Monitor OSFI regulatory developments, emerging practices, and industry trends, advising senior leadership on implications and required actions.
- Track commitments and action plans and provide consolidated reporting on OSFI matters, compliance activities, and progress against regulatory observations to senior management and the Board.
What you should have:
- An undergraduate degree in a related field, such as business, finance or commerce.
- A professional designation in a related field is required (CPA, CRM, FRM).
- A minimum of 7 years of prior relevant experience in compliance and risk governance, especially in the context of relationship with OSFI.
- In-depth knowledge of the area of specialization, industry standards and frameworks, risk management, assurance and oversight.
- Superior written and oral communication skills, including strong influencing and negotiating skills. Ability to deliver a persuasive, clear presentation of ideas that will convince others and gain acceptance of proposals or plans.
- Advanced critical thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills with demonstrated ability to capture and synthesize information to develop recommendations and provide advice.
- The ability to establish and maintain effective and trustworthy working relationships.
- The ability to plan and manage multiple, concurrent priorities, and work under tight time constraints.

Cold Lake The City of Cold Lake is located in Alberta’s Lakeland and nestled on the shore of Alberta’s seventh largest lake. Cold Lake also has modern recreation and sport facilities, a nearby alpine ski hill, as well as urban and rural trail systems. Defence Industrial Strategy
The NRC has an important role within the Government of Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy, accelerating research and innovation, and helping Canadian businesses develop leading-edge technologies for civilian and military use.
With expertise across fields such as transportation, quantum science, medical countermeasures and advanced manufacturing, the NRC is hiring to drive the development of national sovereign defence capabilities. The following role will support the NRC’s contributions to defence priorities.
The role
The NRC is building new capabilities to help Canada accelerate the development, integration and adoption of emerging drone, counter-drone and autonomous systems technologies. At the centre of this effort is the Drone Innovation Hub (DIH) and its Aurora Shield program—bringing together NRC researchers, engineers and facilities with the Canadian Armed Forces, Department of National Defence, industry, academia and other partners to tackle some of Canada's most important defence and security technology challenges.
We are looking for a Senior Project Manager to help turn that ambition into action .
Working alongside the Aurora Shield Program Director, the successful candidate will help shape and deliver a rapidly growing portfolio of research, technology development and innovation activities. This is not a traditional project management role. Individual projects are led by researcher and engineer Project Managers from across the NRC; the Senior Project Manager will work across those projects—helping PMs succeed, maintaining coherence across the portfolio, solving problems and ensuring that the program delivers as a whole.
The role also extends beyond the individual projects. Aurora Shield is developing new ways for NRC, DND, the Canadian Armed Forces and industry to work together, including major ecosystem wide initiatives. The successful candidate will help take these initiatives from ambitious concepts to executable activities—working through the plans, partnerships, budgets, documentation and details required to make them real.
The result is a role with an unusually broad range: from strategy to execution, and from individual projects to the broader Canadian defence innovation ecosystem . On any given day, the Senior Project Manager might help a Project Manager resolve a delivery challenge, work through program budgets and priorities, develop the implementation plan for a new Aurora Shield initiative, prepare material for senior decision-makers, or engage with DND, other government departments and Canadian industry and academia.
We are looking for someone who thrives in that environment—someone who can bring structure to complexity, move comfortably between technical and programmatic discussions, build relationships across organizations, and turn good ideas into delivered outcomes. The Senior Project Manager would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Bachelor or Master’s Degree in engineering management, systems engineering, engineering, business/project management or related discipline.

- Significant* experience managing complex, multi-disciplinary projects or programs involving science, engineering, technology development or innovation;
- Significant* experience working with multi-disciplinary teams of engineers, scientists, technical specialists, project managers and/or business professionals;
- Significant* experience in program or project management, including planning, budgeting, scheduling, risk management, reporting and delivery;
- Experience coordinating a portfolio of related projects or activities and identifying dependencies, risks and opportunities across multiple projects;
- Experience developing detailed implementation plans, project documentation, business cases, proposals, plans or similar products from higher-level concepts or strategic direction; and
- Experience engaging and coordinating with multiple internal and external stakeholders.
Assets:
- Experience in aerospace, defence and security, autonomous systems, drones or other complex technology-development environments;
- Experience working with the Department of National Defence, Canadian Armed Forces, other government departments or the Canadian defence industry;
- Experience with intellectual property, collaborative research agreements, contracting, procurement or other mechanisms supporting complex research and development activities.
*Significant experience is referring to between 2 to 6 years.

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
Help bring research to life and drive your career forward with the National Research Council of Canada (NRC), Canada’s largest research and technology organization.
We are looking for a Bioinformatics Support Specialist to join the Aquatic and Crop Resource Development (ACRD) Research Centre in Halifax, Nova Scotia. This is an opportunity to apply your bioinformatics expertise to meaningful research in environmental genomics, toxicogenomics, bioprospecting, and algal biotechnology, while working with multidisciplinary teams across government, academia, and industry. The incumbent would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The successful candidate will develop, implement, and maintain reproducible bioinformatics workflows and computational tools to process, analyze, and interpret high-throughput sequencing data, including genomics, transcriptomics, metabarcoding, and metagenomics datasets.
Working under the direction of a Team Lead, the Bioinformatics Support Specialist will contribute to the development and validation of genomic platforms, including zebrafish transcriptomics models for toxicological risk assessment, and its relevance to human-specific outcomes. Their role will also support research that advances our understanding of biological responses to environmental change, pollutants, climate change, and other stressors in aquatic and marine ecosystems, with a particular focus on the analysis of microbial and algal communities.
The Bioinformatics Support Specialist will:
- Provide bioinformatics support for the analysis and interpretation of functional genomics data, with an emphasis on RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq).
- Provide bioinformatics support for the analysis of genomic, metagenomic, metabarcoding, and other high-throughput DNA sequencing datasets.
- Develop, implement, maintain, and document reproducible bioinformatics workflows and computational pipelines for omics data analysis.
- Maintain accurate documentation of analytical workflows, methods, and results, and communicate findings effectively through written reports and oral presentations.
- Prepare and contribute to scientific publications, technical reports, conference presentations, and other knowledge dissemination activities.
- Conceive and initiate computational biology projects, contribute to grant and funding proposals, and collaborate with a broad range of internal and external partners.
- Contribute to ACRD's multidisciplinary research environment by providing technical expertise, supporting collaborative research projects, and mentoring researchers and trainees as appropriate.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
B.Sc. or M.Sc in Computer Science combined with extensive experience in biological applications or M.Sc. in Life Sciences combined with strong demonstrated computer science/bioinformatics skills.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Significant* experience managing, processing, and analyzing next-generation sequencing (NGS) data generated using Illumina and/or Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing platforms.
- Significant* experience developing, implementing, and maintaining reproducible bioinformatics workflows for DNA sequence (genomic and metagenomics), including quality control and processing, assembly, taxonomic classification and bioprospecting to identify novel genes, metabolic pathways, and bioactive compounds.
- Significant* experience developing, implementing and maintaining complete RNAseq workflow from sequencing data to downstream analysis.
- Experience** using bioinformatics software and tools for DNA/RNA sequence analysis and manipulation in Linux/Unix environments.
- Experience** programming and scripting for bioinformatics applications using one or more languages such as Python, R, Bash (Unix shell), Perl, Java, or C/C++.
- Experience** using version control systems (e.g., Git) and working in high-performance computing (HPC) or cloud computing environments is considered an asset .
- Experience** documenting bioinformatics workflows and providing technical support or training to users is considered an asset .
*Significant experience is defined as three (3) or more years of experience. **Experience is defined as one (1) or more years of experience.

Reliability Status

English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests

Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Advanced knowledge of the development and implementation and maintenance of reproducible genomic/transcriptomic/metagenomic bioinformatics workflows, including web-based tools, algorithms, pipelines, software solutions and database resources in the area of bioinformatics for data manipulation and analysis.
- Advanced understanding of Linux/Unix fundamentals and using command-line tools as applied to systems administration and bioinformatics software development in a distributed and heterogeneous Linux environment.
- Ability to download/manipulate raw sequence data (including quality control and processing), alignment/generation count matrices using STAR (or equivalent), statistical correction of count data (DESeq2 or equivalent) and generation of downstream input files for ontological analysis using web-based approaches, development of data analysis methods, identifying human orthologs of differentially expressed genes, and mapping to transcriptome atlases.
- Ability to process and analyze data, compose draft reports, protocols and standard operating procedures, and contribute to the preparation of research publications and client reports.
- Ability to analyze and discuss technical issues, troubleshoot and solve problems relating to application to bioinformatics.
- Ability to program and script for bioinformatics applications using one or more languages such as Python, R, Bash (Unix shell), Perl, Java, or C/C++. Ability to work in high-performance computing (HPC) or cloud computing environments is considered an asset .

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
The NRC is seeking a senior research executive to fulfil the role of Director General (DG), to lead the Aquatic and Crop Resource Development Research Centre and make up the ranks of its senior management team.
The incoming DG’s goal will be to lead and inspire a diverse multisite and multidisciplinary team to excel in performing advanced scientific research and technology development supporting Canada’s food system productivity, primarily through sustainable transformation of Canadian agricultural and marine bioresources.
ACRD’s largest site is in Saskatoon and it is focused on application of innovative technology and data-driven approaches to design crops that are resilient to environmental stressors and can be cultivated in northern and remote locations. ACRD’s research interests include integrating engineering, intelligent systems, data analytics, and plant biotechnology to optimize crop production in controlled indoor environments. Strategic collaborations with industry, plant breeders and other regional stakeholders, including the provincial government and academic institutions, are critical. In addition, ACRD is investing in modernizing its R&D infrastructure, including a digital transformation, to fulfil the ambition of being a globally-relevant crop design technology accelerator.
ACRD also contributes to Canada’s blue bioeconomy through applied research that advances marine bioresource valorization, sustainable aquatic production systems, and the scale-up of marine bioproducts, while promoting environmental stewardship and community and stakeholder partnerships. This work is enabled by ACRD’s Marine Research Station in Ketch Harbour, NS, where microalgae, seaweeds, and other marine and freshwater organisms are cultivated, as well as by analytical and bioproduct-development laboratories in Halifax.
The role, Continued
Complementing these areas of focus is ACRD’s Atypical Fermentation Facility (AFF), as well as associated analytical and downstream processing capacity in Charlottetown. It anchors an industrial biomanufacturing innovation hub in the burgeoning PEI biotech ecosystem, to support the commercialization of bio-based products.
Reporting to the Vice-President, Research (Life Sciences), the Director General, Aquatic and Crop Resource Development (DG, ACRD) provides strategic leadership on matters relating to agricultural and biomarine research across the NRC and works closely with internal and external stakeholders in advancing its research agenda. The DG strategically positions on-going and new projects while spearheading growth initiatives and research collaborations with industry, academia, and government partners to develop and transform agricultural and marine bioresources into food, feed and ingredients, and other high value bioproducts.
As a well-qualified candidate, you are a seasoned research leader and come with a high level of scientific credibility in one or more of the centre’s disciplines. You are skilled in inspiring research groups and collaborating across the innovation landscape in achieving outcomes. You bring significant experience in developing, maintaining, and leveraging strategic partnerships, research collaborations and client relationships that include academia, SME’s, and governmental research bodies. You are experienced in developing and leading research strategies designed to keep groups at the forefront of scientific and technical fields. As an outstanding communicator you easily navigate large, complex organizations with many stakeholders, and are skilled in developing high performing teams that pivot to seize emerging opportunities and adapt to change. As an ideal candidate, you possess a master’s or PhD in a relevant field.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
An advanced post secondary degree such as Ph.D. and/or MSc/MBA with significant experience leading research teams in a relevant field. Preference may be given to candidates with a combination of science and business education.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Significant experience conducting original research in a field related to the position and ideally recognition as a global leader in their domain of expertise.
- Significant experience supervising and developing staff in multidisciplinary teams, ideally in a matrix environment of projects and programs.
- Significant and recently demonstrated experience in applying the principles, tools and practices of leadership, administrative, financial, and human resource management.
- Experience managing multidisciplinary R&D programs.
- Significant and demonstrated scientific or engineering and technical leadership.
- Significant experience in building partnerships with national and international organizations.
- Experience developing and maintaining strategic projects with senior government officials, academic and industry leaders.
- Senior executive experience including a demonstrated ability to lead change, build superior teams, motivate a diverse group of individuals, and direct large-scale initiatives.
Condition of employment
Secret clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
Language requirements
Bilingual Imperative CBC/CBC
Note: In the event that no qualified bilingual candidates are identified, NRC may consider unilingual candidates who will be required to commit to achieving these levels within two years.
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Strong knowledge of the national and international Aquatic and Crop Resource Development’s research community.
- Knowledge of the Canadian innovation process, the structure of the Canadian research and innovation systems, and the Canadian research community.
- Ability to effectively lead and manage a multi-faceted organization in an R&D environment with a style and approach that supports NRC’s commitment to scientific excellence and its participative management and entrepreneurship values.\Demonstrated ability to successfully leverage, government, industry or other partnerships to generate and deliver on ideas that would lead to recognition of NRC’s role in world-wide research and technology innovation.
- Strong knowledge of Aquatic and Crop Resource Development’s initiatives, programs and activities and their potential for impact nationally and internationally.
- Recognized leadership in the field of aquatic and crop resource development.
- Ability to analyze complex information, make timely decisions and communicate clearly with all internal and external stakeholders.
- Ability to manage in a scientific environment with in depth knowledge of the different models of research operations while enhancing a collaborative approach.
- Knowledge of the National Research Council, its mandate and strategic objectives.
Behavioural competencies
- Management Competencies (MG) - Inspirational Leadership (Level 4)
- Management Competencies (MG) - Self-Awareness (3)
- Management Competencies (MG) - Strategic Outlook and Alignment (Level 4)
- Management Competencies (MG) - Drive for Results and Efficiency (Level 4)
- Management Competencies (MG) - Leverage Collaborative Relationships (Level 4)
- Management Competencies (MG) - Client Relationship Management (Level 4)
- Management Competencies (MG) - Service Orientation (level 4)
- Management Competencies (MG) - Financial Management (Level 4)
- Management Competencies (MG) - Human Resources Management (4)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Management Competencies (MG)
View all competency profiles
Compensation
From $189,203 to $226,920 per annum.
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Notes

The Director General of MDRC will inspire and lead Bioengineering Technologies R&D focused on advancing innovation in the area of microfluidic-based point-of-care (POC) diagnostics and virtual health digital technologies.
MDRC’s largest site is located in Boucherville, Montreal which includes a Biodevice scale-up foundry and virtual health technologies expertise and facilities. MDRC also has a satellite presence at the University of Toronto, which includes MDRC’s flagship collaboration centre and initiative – CRAFT (Centre for Research and Applications in Fluidic Technologies). The Mint is hiring a Senior Program Manager, Program Management Office (PMO) who can thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment.
Reporting to the Director, PMO, the Senior Program Manager, PMO is responsible for successful project, program management and change management within the PMO at the Mint by working closely with partners throughout the organization to execute and deliver on projects using best practices and PMO standards. This role will be accountable for the development and delivery of complex plans and processes to deliver on priority work with multi-faceted business objectives. The role will optimize and influence the coordination of project resources to ensure that work objectives are consistently met and that the work can achieve operational/organizational excellence. The incumbent will provide professional services at a senior working level and contribute to providing advice and functional direction on matters in project management and change management.
Your Responsibilities:
- Provide project and program management services for specific complex projects, tasks, or initiatives.
- Work with other senior management of PMO to contribute to building stronger standards within the RCM for project management and change management.
- Ensure excellent communication and relationships exist between PMO and business partners throughout the organization.
- Strategize on methodologies and approaches to use for specific complex projects, tasks or initiatives.
- Support growth and strengthening of PMO standards, toolkit, communications and tactical execution.
- Provide expert advice to PMO colleagues on organizational culture and insight on business functionality to better execute projects.
This position offers a hybrid work arrangement, requiring on-site presence at our Winnipeg location three to five days per week, depending on meeting requirements and other activities.
This selection process may also qualify you for other positions with similar requirements and qualifications.
Qualifications:
Languages Requirements:
Proficiency in English is essential. Proficiency in Mandarin is considered an asset.
Education & Designation:
- University degree in related area.
- Must hold valid PMP certification
- Prosci certification preferred.
Experience:
- Minimum of 10 years of related business experience.
Additional Qualifications:
- Must have experience in manufacturing and technology projects.
- Knowledge of project management best practices, methodologies, and tactics.
- Knowledge of change management best practices, methodologies and tactics.
- Proficient in MS Project, Azure DevOps, MS Office Suite.
- Skilled presentation skills, in both development of materials and presenting to senior leaders.
- Ability to leverage organizational values, objectives and culture to strategize towards project success.
Why the Mint?
At the Mint, you will collaborate with a diverse group of people and be a part of an iconic Canadian organization. Your safety and wellbeing are our top priority. We offer outstanding pay and total rewards for you and your family and you will be supported to continuously learn throughout your career.
The Mint is committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We value diversity and aim to provide an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment, selection and onboarding process to ensure that each candidate is treated respectfully. In accordance with the Employment Equity Act, you are invited to voluntarily self-identify with one or more of the four employment equity groups (women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities and members of visible minorities) by sending your application to the confidential email, EE@mint.ca that is accessed only by the Human Resources section.
If you need accommodation at any point in the application or interview process, please let us know. We are committed to being an inclusive employer. For a confidential inquiry, simply email us directly at EE@mint.ca to make arrangements.
W hat to Expect:
In order to be considered for an interview, please clearly demonstrate on your application how you meet the language, education and experience qualifications. The additional qualifications may be assessed through interviews, exams, reference checks, etc.
Selected candidates will be required to complete a background check facilitated by the Mint in order to obtain a security clearance.
Ready to mint your career? Please forward your resume to careers@mint.ca by October 5, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!

The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) is an independent agency of the Government of Canada, dedicated to fostering public trust and confidence in Canada's financial system by rigorously regulating and supervising over 400 federally regulated financial institutions (FRFIs) and 1200 federally regulated pension plans (FRPPs). OSFI has offices located in 4 major cities across Canada: Ottawa, Toronto, Montreal and Vancouver. Safeguarding Canada’s Financial Future: Through diligent regulation and supervision of FRFIs and FRPPs, we ensure that these entities operate soundly and securely. Our proactive approach to risk management and early intervention safeguards the interests of depositors, policyholders, pension plan members, and beneficiaries. We remain committed to fostering public confidence and supporting the competitive and resilient nature of Canada's financial landscape. Our Mandate: Our mandate is to ensure the stability and integrity of Canada's financial system. We achieve this by: Maintaining Financial Soundness: Ensuring that FRFIs and FRPPs remain in sound financial condition. Safeguarding Against Threats: Ensuring that FRFIs protect themselves against threats to their integrity and security, including foreign interference. Proactive Intervention: Acting swiftly when issues arise, requiring FRFIs and FRPPs to implement necessary corrective measures without delay. Risk Management: Continuously monitoring and evaluating risks, promoting sound risk management practices among FRFIs and FRPPs. Our Approach: In fulfilling our mandate, we adopt a balanced approach: For FRFIs: We protect the rights and interests of depositors, policyholders, and financial institution creditors. At the same time, we recognize the need for FRFIs to compete effectively and take reasonable risks. For FRPPs: We safeguard the rights and interests of pension plan members, former members, and entitled beneficiaries. Join Us: Be part of a system that ensures financial stability and security for all Canadians. Learn more about our work and how you can contribute to a stronger Canadian financial future. Follow Us: Twitter: @OSFICanada LinkedIn: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions Canada

This role requires an individual who can seamlessly transition between strategic architecture, technical leadership, and hands-on troubleshooting.

- Provide hands-on technical delivery, including D365 configuration, workflow optimization, system design, implementation, testing, deployments, production support, and incident resolution.
- Review code and technical solutions, maintain architecture and operational documentation, mentor technical teams, and communicate complex concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- A strong knowledge of the Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, and Dataverse.
- A proven experience designing and implementing enterprise integration architectures and patterns.
- A strong proficiency with REST and SOAP APIs and enterprise integration technologies.
- An experience with Azure Integration Services, Azure Logic Apps, Service Bus, and event-driven architectures.
- An expertise in data integration, synchronization, and troubleshooting distributed systems and complex production environments.
- A solid understanding of security, authentication, authorization, enterprise architecture principles, and experience working in Agile and DevOps environments.

- Microsoft Dynamics 365 certifications.

- Experience with enterprise middleware platforms.
- Experience supporting highly integrated and mission-critical business platforms.
- Knowledge of data architecture, analytics, and reporting solutions.
